result.title: The Most Capable Humanoid Robot Yet!
result.description:
Google just released Gemini Robotics 2 today, and it's a much bigger leap than you may think.

Unlike previous models, it coordinates everything from feet to fingertips, allowing the robot to balance and walk while handling delicate objects.

With 22 degrees of movement in its hands, it can seal Ziploc bags, unscrew lightbulbs, and even tie trash bag knots.

Plus, an on-device version runs locally without an internet connection and can adapt to new robot bodies in just a few hours.

To be clear: this new release "Google Robotics 2" is the AI software behind the robot, not a physical robot you buy directly from Google. It powers hardware from partners like Apptronik on their Apollo 2 robot. 

For Developers: You can access the reasoning model "Gemini Robotics ER 2" today on Google AI Studio.
For Hardware Integrators: The full Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and On-Device models are currently available to partners through Google DeepMind's early access program.

#Google #deepmind #robotics #futuretech #ainews

result.title: I can't believe Claude figured this out
result.description:
I gave Claude Code a random photo with zero geotags and it searched the web to figure out where it was taken 🤯

Anthropic recently launched a native, sandboxed in-app browser built directly into Claude Code on desktop that can open a real browser pane beside your workspace. It can read web pages, click links, and interact with elements—making it incredibly useful for researching documentation, debugging, or building web tools side-by-side.

Here's how to access and try it yourself 👇
- Open up Claude Code Desktop.
- Press Cmd + Shift + B on macOS (or Ctrl + Shift + B on Windows) to open the built-in browser panel.
- Give Claude a task that requires web research, live testing, or coding based on web resources, and watch it work in real time.

📁 Save this reel so you can reference these steps later, and follow for more updates, hands-on tutorials, and practical AI use cases!

result.title: Literally everyone hated this feature
result.description:
Did Meta actually think we wouldn’t notice this? 🫣

Recently, Meta rolled out a new image-generation feature called Muse Image. On paper, it was pitched as a creative new AI tool. In reality, it turned into a massive privacy and safety concern overnight.

By default, the feature automatically opted in public accounts, allowing anyone to simply @ a handle and use Meta AI to generate entirely new images using that person's likeness with NO permission required.

Unsurprisingly, after immense backlash from users, privacy advocates, and talent agencies, Meta pulled the feature just three days after launch.

But this whole ordeal leaves us with a pretty big question… did Meta genuinely not anticipate this backlash, or was this a calculated move to get eyes on their new AI model?

Let me know which one you think it is in the comments. 👇

#AI #Ainews #genAI
